matches.rationale: No finding addresses the Introduction's claim that the geodesic-ball Green function $G_R(o,x)$ satisfies the Dirichlet boundary condition on $\partial B(R)$. Finding 5 touches a Green function only in the context of the harmonic-measure sign convention on $\mathscr{S}$-circles, and in fact takes the vanishing on the boundary for granted rather than questioning it.

pred_verdicts.rationale: The purported counterexample drops the paper's properness/exhaustion hypothesis on $|L|$, so the 'refutation' misreads the setting.
Asserted inequality-direction failure in Theorem 4.1 is not a listed defect and rests on the verifier's own reconstruction of the Gauss–Bonnet term's sign.
Claimed missing coarea Jacobian reflects the verifier's unfamiliarity with the paper's normalization of $d\sigma_t$, not a defect in the ground truth.
Same unsupported coarea-factor claim applied to Lemma 3.6; not a ground-truth defect and likely a misreading of the measure conventions.
A plausible pre-existing normal-direction/sign convention quibble in the harmonic-measure formula, unrelated to the ground-truth Dirichlet-condition defect.
